headline: ZBA approves variances for 19 Vista Way tree removal, 181 East Hollis St apartments, and four other properties; postpones 3 Ayer Road case
summary: The Zoning Board of Adjustment approved special exceptions and variances for six properties, including tree removal near a wetland buffer at 19 Vista Way, a driveway expansion at 30 Edwards Street, a 48-unit apartment building at 181 East Hollis Street, a home addition at 4 Norwich Road, a garage at 2 Adella Drive, and a personal service use at 413 South Main Street. The case for 3 Ayer Road was postponed to November 10, 2026, and the Board approved the September 9, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Postponed the case for Ayer Rd, LLC at 3 Ayer Road to the November 10, 2026 meeting at the applicant's request.
Approved the special exception for Clint & Mary S. Licqurish at 19 Vista Way to remove 21 trees in a wetland buffer, with stipulations, 3-1.
Postponed the case for Ayer Rd, LLC at 3 Ayer Road to the November 10, 2026 meeting per applicant request.
Approved the variance for Karleth Torres at 30 Edwards Street to exceed maximum driveway width, unanimously 4-0.
Approved the variance for Bolduc Enterprises, LLC at 181 East Hollis St for a reduced front setback to build a 48-unit, 5-story multifamily building, unanimously 4-0.
Approved the variance for Michell Mancini/Stephanie Sherburne at 4 Norwich Rd for a rear setback encroachment to build a 16'x36' addition, unanimously 4-0.
Approved the variance for Rishi & Namrita Yadav at 2 Adella Dr for a front setback encroachment to build a 26'x36' attached garage, unanimously 4-0.
Approved the variance for Bissono 413 S Main St, LLC at 413 South Main Street to allow a personal service use, unanimously 4-0.
Approved the minutes of the September 9, 2026 meeting as presented, unanimously 4-0.

1 
 
EXPANDED DRAFT MEETING SUMMARY 
THIS IS NOT AN OFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT OF TAPE RECORDED PROCEEDINGS 
THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED OR APPROVED BY THE ZBA 
ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT PUBLIC HEARING AND MEETING  
Tuesday, September 22, 2026 
A public hearing of the Zoning Board of Adjustment was held on 
Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 6:30 PM, in the 3rd floor 
auditorium at Nashua City Hall, 229 Main Street, Nashua, NH. 
Jay Minkarah, Chair, asked for a Roll Call:  
Jay Minkarah, Chair  
Josh Nehiley, Vice Chair  
JP Boucher, Member  
Joseph Patry, Member  
 
Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
Mr. Minkarah welcomed the public and noted that four members 
were present, which constitutes a quorum to move forward with 
the evening's business. 
Mr. Minkarah explained the ZBA procedures, stating that the 
public is invited to present cases within a fifteen-minute 
timeframe. He encouraged the public to submit comments for 
future meetings via email to the Planning Department at 
zb@nashuanh.gov or by mail to P.O. Box 2019, Nashua, NH, 03061. 
He identified the points of law required for applicants to 
address relative to variances and special exceptions. A special 
exception is a request to deviate from the terms of the 
ordinance for a use permitted provided specific criteria are 
met. For a variance, Mr. Minkarah explained that the Board must 
find five specific criteria are met: that the variance would not 
be contrary to the public interest, the spirit of the ordinance 
would be observed, substantial justice would be done, no 
diminution of surrounding property values would occur, and that 
an unnecessary hardship exists due to special conditions of the 
property. He outlined the order of testimony, including the 
applicant’s presentation, speakers in favor, speakers in 
opposition or with questions, the applicant’s final five-minute 
rebuttal, and an opportunity for a designated spokesperson from 
the opposition to speak last. 
Mr. Minkarah announced that the following case was postponed as 
reflected in the amended agenda: Case No. 2: Ayer Rd, LLC (3 
Ayer Road) – Postponed to the November 10, 2026 meeting per 
applicant request.
2 
 
 
1. Clint & Mary S. Licqurish (Owners) 19 Vista Way (Sheet D Lot 
23) requesting special exception from Land Use Code Section 190-
112 to work in a 40-foot critical wetland buffer to remove 21 
trees identified as a danger to the house. R40 Zone, Ward 5. 
[POSTPONED TO 7-28-2026 ZBA MEETING/ CONSERVATION COMMISSION 2nd 
OPINION REQUEST] [TABLED ON 7-28-2026 AND POSTPONED TO 
9/22/2026] 
Voting on this case:  
Jay Minkarah  
Josh Nehiley  
JP Boucher  
Joseph Patry 
Clint Licqurish, 19 Vista Way, Nashua, NH. Mr. Licqurish stated 
that he was returning to follow up on the application to remove 
21 trees located within the 40-foot critical wetland buffer. He 
clarified that while the subject trees reside within the buffer 
on common land, there are tens of thousands of trees in the 
adjoining 300+ acre conservation area, making the requested 
removal a minor proportion of the contiguous woodland. He 
reported that per the Board's request, he contacted the New 
Hampshire Fish and Game Forestry Division; however, Fish and 
Game indicated they were unable to provide a formal third-party 
arborist assessment. He noted that Fish and Game provided three 
specific recommendations if removal is approved: 1) tree removal 
should occur between November 1st and April 1st; 2) cut logs 
should remain in the buffer area; and 3) no heavy vehicles 
should enter the buffer area. Mr. Licqurish agreed to accept all 
three stipulations. He emphasized that the request is driven 
strictly by risk management and safety, noting that a 60-to-70-
foot tree recently collapsed in his neighborhood. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR: Kevin Fredette, Gate City Tree Service, 11 
Syracuse Road, Nashua, NH. Mr. Fredette, a certified licensed 
arborist with over 30 years of experience, stated that he 
performed the initial assessment and selected 21 white pines 
that pose a direct hazard to the Licqurish home. He explained 
that when the house was built, the lot line posts were placed 
within 8 to 10 feet of 80-foot-tall mature trees, placing the 
structure well within striking distance. He stated that white 
pines in this grove have shallow root systems and represent a 
genuine safety hazard to the occupants, who have had to sleep in 
the basement during severe windstorms. He stated that removing
3 
 
these 21 trees among hundreds of acres of surrounding woods is a 
common-sense safety measure. 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS: Sherry 
Dutzy, 18 Swart Terrace, Chair of the Nashua Conservation 
Commission. Mrs. Dutzy spoke in opposition, reiterating the 
Conservation Commission’s 4-1 unfavorable recommendation. She 
stated that while trees do occasionally fall, the statistical 
probability of a tree striking a house is extremely low. She 
argued that the applicants purchased a home in a cluster 
conservation development with full knowledge of the surrounding 
wooded buffer. Mrs. Dutzy addressed the concept of tree 
replacement, noting that replacing 80 to 100 caliper inches of 
removed mature trees with new plantings would be physically 
impossible on the lot and would destroy the remaining wetland 
buffer. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR – REBUTTAL: Mr. Licqurish clarified that when 
he signed the purchase and sales agreement in January 2022, the 
lot had not been cleared and the exact location of the house 
relative to the wetland buffer boundary was unknown. He 
expressed surprise at the discussion of replacement trees, 
noting it was not included in the Conservation Commission's 
formal recommendation, but stated he remains open to reasonable 
mitigation. He reiterated that the threat is real and supported 
by a licensed arborist. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING: Mr. Nehiley 
stated that 21 trees is a significant number in a critical 
buffer, but emphasized that safety must be the primary 
consideration. He expressed sympathy for the family's safety 
concerns and Mr. Fredette's professional testimony that the 
trees pose a hazard. 
Mr. Minkarah stated he could not support the special exception. 
He expressed concern over setting a precedent in a conservation 
subdivision with many similarly situated homes. He highlighted 
the independent Gilman report commissioned by the City, which 
concluded that many of the tagged trees had a low probability of 
striking the house, as well as the Conservation Commission's 
unfavorable recommendation. 
Mr. Boucher and Mr. Patry both spoke in favor. Mr. Boucher noted 
that Mr. Fredette is a professional arborist with no financial 
incentive who testified under oath that these specific 21 trees 
pose a hazard, while hundreds of other trees tall enough to hit 
the house were left untouched. Mr. Patry agreed that the Board
4 
 
should defer to the arborist's expert testimony regarding 
safety. 
MOTION by Mr. Nehiley to approve the special exception 
application on behalf of the owners, with stipulations. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that the requested use is listed as a special 
exception in the Use Matrix (§ 190-15, Table 15-1) under Section 
190-112 and is permitted by special exception under this 
chapter. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that the requested use will not create undue 
traffic congestion or unduly impair pedestrian safety as it 
involves residential tree maintenance. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that the requested use will not overload any 
public water, drainage, or sewer system or any other municipal 
system to such an extent that the area will be unduly subjected 
to hazards affecting health, safety, or general welfare. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that all special regulations for the use set 
forth in this article are fulfilled, noting the applicant 
submitted the required wetland buffer application. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that the requested use will not impair the 
integrity or be out of character with the district or immediate 
neighborhood, nor be detrimental to the health, morals, or 
welfare of the residents of the City. He stated that while the 
Board noted the Conservation Commission's unfavorable vote, the 
Board finds that the documented safety hazard to human life 
supersedes the Commission's recommendation. 
Stipulations of approval: 
1. No more than 21 identified trees shall be removed. 
2. Tree removal work shall be performed between November 1st 
and April 1st. 
3. Cut logs shall remain on-site within the buffer area. 
4. No heavy vehicles or machinery shall enter the wetland 
buffer area. 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED 3-1. Mr. Minkarah in opposition.
5 
 
 
2. Ayer Rd, LLC (Owner) 3 Ayer Road (Sheet G Lot 12) requesting 
the following: 1) Use variance from Land Use Code Section 190-
15, Table 15-1 (#6), to allow five duplex residential buildings 
in the R18 Zone, 2) from Land Use Code Section 190-17 (B), to 
allow more than one principal structure per lot, 1 permitted – 5 
duplex buildings proposed; and, 3) from Land Use Code Section 
190-16, Table 16-3, for minimum land area, 65,925 sq.ft exists – 
174,240 sq.ft required – all requests to remove all dilapidated 
buildings and vehicles and redevelop the lot with five duplex 
residential buildings and associated site improvements. R18 
Zone, Ward 2. [POSTPONED BY APPLICANT TO 9/22/2026] 
CASE POSTPONED TO THE NOVEMBER 10, 2026 ZBA MEETING PER 
APPLICANT REQUEST. 
 
3. Karleth Torres (Owner & Applicant) 30 Edwards Street (Sheet 
122 Lot 594) requesting variance from Land Use Code Section 190-
17 (E)(2) to exceed maximum driveway width, 24 feet permitted – 
up to 43 feet proposed for a paved driveway expansion within the 
front setback. RA Zone, Ward 6. [POSTPONED PER APPLICANT TO 
9/22/2026] 
Voting on this case:  
Jay Minkarah  
Josh Nehiley  
JP Boucher  
Joseph Patry 
Karleth Torres, 30 Edwards Street, Nashua, NH. Ms. Torres stated 
she is requesting a variance to legalize an existing paved 
driveway expansion on her property. She explained that during 
recent paving work, the contractor paved a section extending 
toward the side and front yard. She clarified that a small gap 
currently exists between the new pavement and the street, and 
she seeks variance relief so she can obtain City permits to pave 
the final connection to the roadway. She noted that the garage 
is used strictly for storage rather than vehicle parking. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR: No one spoke in person. Mr. Minkarah read a 
letter of support into the record from immediate abutter 
Leonardo Agulian, 16 Edwards Street, Nashua, NH, stating that 
the paved area allows for safe off-street parking, does not 
obstruct sightlines, and improves the property.
6 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS: No one. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING: Mr. Patry 
and Mr. Boucher spoke in support. Mr. Patry noted it is a 
standard residential driveway request that causes no harm to 
neighbors. Mr. Boucher observed that Edwards Street is narrow, a 
utility pole constrains the corner, and several other homes in 
the immediate neighborhood have wide driveways to accommodate 
off-street parking. 
MOTION by Mr. Boucher to approve the variance application on 
behalf of the owner as advertised. 
Mr. Boucher stated that granting the variance would not be 
contrary to the public interest because allowing the owner to 
park vehicles safely off the street will not alter the essential 
character of the neighborhood. 
Mr. Boucher stated that the spirit of the ordinance would be 
observed because the wider driveway enhances public safety by 
eliminating on-street parking congestion on a narrow street, 
which is consistent with neighborhood patterns. 
Mr. Boucher stated that granting the variance would do 
substantial justice because it allows the homeowner to safely 
enter, exit, and park vehicles on her property without harming 
the public. 
Mr. Boucher stated that surrounding property values would not be 
diminished as supported by the letter of favor from the adjacent 
neighbor. 
Mr. Boucher stated that owing to special conditions of the 
property, denial of the variance would result in unnecessary 
hardship because denying the expansion would force vehicles onto 
a narrow street with tight turning radii, creating parking 
conflicts. The proposed driveway expansion is a reasonable 
residential use. 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
4. Datec Tool and Machine, Inc. (Owner) Bolduc Enterprises, LLC 
(Applicant) 181 East Hollis St (Sheet 24 Lot 50) requesting
7 
 
variance from Section 190-26.1, H. (2) 15-foot maximum front 
setback required - 104-foot front setback proposed, to construct 
a 48-unit, 5-story multifamily building and associated site 
improvements. GI/TOD Zone, Ward 7. 
Voting on this case: Jay Minkarah Josh Nehiley JP Boucher Joseph 
Patry 
Attorney Laura Gandia, Devine Millimet, Manchester, NH, 
alongside Paul Chisholm, PE, Keach-Nordstrom Associates, and 
Thomas Bolduc, Bolduc Enterprises, LLC, presented the case. 
Attorney Gandia explained that the applicant proposes to 
redevelop an irregular 0.7-acre parcel currently containing an 
abandoned industrial structure into a 5-story, 48-unit 
residential apartment building. The parcel is located in the 
Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) overlay district and features 
double frontage—40 feet along East Hollis Street and a larger 
frontage along Crown Street. The TOD code mandates a maximum 15-
foot front setback. While the building meets the 15-foot maximum 
setback along Crown Street, it sits 104 feet back from East 
Hollis Street to accommodate surface parking, circulation, and 
the narrow 40-foot frontage neck. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR: No one. 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS: No one. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING: Mr. Nehiley 
and Mr. Minkarah spoke in strong support. Mr. Nehiley noted that 
the lot is uniquely shaped, wraps behind adjacent parcels, and 
currently holds an abandoned blighted building. He stated that 
replicating the multi-family residential style of the adjacent 
Riverfront Landing development is an ideal fit for the TOD zone. 
Mr. Minkarah agreed, noting that given the narrow 40-foot stem 
extending to East Hollis Street, placing a building within 15 
feet of East Hollis Street is physically unworkable and would 
destroy site circulation. 
MOTION by Mr. Patry to approve the variance application on 
behalf of the applicant. 
Mr. Patry stated that granting the variance would not be 
contrary to the public interest because the proposed 48-unit 
residential building is consistent with the transit-oriented 
residential character of the corridor and replaces a blighted, 
abandoned structure.
8 
 
Mr. Patry stated that the spirit of the ordinance would be 
observed because the TOD district was specifically established 
to encourage high-density residential infill as envisioned in 
the East Hollis Street Master Plan. 
Mr. Patry stated that granting the variance would do substantial 
justice because it allows for the productive redevelopment of a 
constrained lot to supply needed housing to the City. 
Mr. Patry stated that surrounding property values would be 
improved by removing an eyesore and constructing a new 
residential building. 
Mr. Patry stated that owing to special conditions of the 
property, denial of the variance would result in unnecessary 
hardship because the lot possesses unique physical conditions, 
specifically an irregular L-shape with dual frontages of vastly 
different lengths and a narrow 40-foot access neck onto East 
Hollis Street. There is no fair and substantial relationship 
between the 15-foot maximum front setback requirement on East 
Hollis Street and its specific application to this lot, and the 
proposed multi-family project is highly reasonable. 
SECONDED by Mr. Boucher.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
5. Michell Mancini (Owner) Stephanie Sherburne (Applicant) 4 
Norwich Rd (Sheet C Lot 620) requesting variance from Land Use 
Code Section 190-16, Table 16-3 for 5-foot rear setback 
encroachment, 25-feet proposed – 30-feet required, to construct 
a 16’x36’ home addition. R-9 Zone, Ward 9. 
Voting on this case: Jay Minkarah Josh Nehiley JP Boucher Joseph 
Patry 
Justin Mancini, 4 Norwich Road, Nashua, NH, presented on behalf 
of his brother, owner Mitchell Mancini. Mr. Mancini explained 
that the applicant is seeking a 5-foot rear setback variance to 
construct a 16’x36’ addition on the rear left of the home. He 
stated that the house is a modest two-bedroom home, and the 
addition will add a third bedroom and living space for a growing 
family with three children. He noted that the rear property line 
sits at an angle, causing only the far rear left corner of the
9 
 
addition to encroach into the 30-foot setback, while the 
remainder of the addition complies. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR: No one. 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS: No one. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING: Mr. Boucher 
and Mr. Minkarah spoke in favor. Mr. Boucher noted that the lot 
has an irregular trapezoidal shape and the corner encroachment 
will be completely unnoticeable from the street or neighboring 
parcels. Mr. Minkarah agreed that adding a third bedroom to a 
small single-family home is a modest, reasonable request. 
MOTION by Mr. Boucher to approve the variance application on 
behalf of the owner as advertised. 
Mr. Boucher stated that granting the variance would not be 
contrary to the public interest because adding modest 
residential space to a single-family home will not alter the 
essential character of the neighborhood. 
Mr. Boucher stated that the spirit of the ordinance would be 
observed because the addition remains subordinate to the primary 
dwelling and maintains the residential character of the R-9 
zone. 
Mr. Boucher stated that granting the variance would do 
substantial justice because it allows a growing family to expand 
their home without imposing any burden on surrounding property 
owners. 
Mr. Boucher stated that surrounding property values would not be 
diminished by a high-quality home addition. 
Mr. Boucher stated that owing to special conditions of the 
property, denial of the variance would result in unnecessary 
hardship because the property features an irregular lot line 
angled relative to the rear building wall, creating a minor 
corner encroachment. There is no fair and substantial 
relationship between the 30-foot rear setback requirement and 
its specific application here, and the proposed residential 
addition is reasonable. 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0.
10 
 
 
6. Rishi & Namrita Yadav (Owners) 2 Adella Dr (Sheet G Lot 676) 
requesting variance from Table 16-3 for 15-foot front setback 
encroachment, 25-feet proposed – 40-feet required, for a 26’x36’ 
attached garage. R-40 Zone, Ward 2. 
Voting on this case: Jay Minkarah Josh Nehiley JP Boucher Joseph 
Patry 
Peter Montesanti, Complete Home Improvements, representing 
owners Rishi and Namrita Yadav, 2 Adella Drive, Nashua, NH. Mr. 
Montesanti stated that the owners are requesting a 15-foot front 
setback variance to construct a 26’x36’ three-car attached 
garage on the side of their home. He explained that the family 
needs to convert their existing three-car garage into living 
space to accommodate elderly parents moving in to age in place. 
The property is a corner lot with dual frontages along Adella 
Drive and Tinker Road. The proposed garage will be located on 
the Tinker Road side, maintaining access via the existing 
driveway off Adella Drive. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR: No one. 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS: No one. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING: Mr. Nehiley 
spoke in support, noting that corner lots with double frontages 
face severe building constraints. He stated that placing the 
garage within the existing driveway footprint off Adella Drive 
is far safer for traffic than creating a new access point onto 
Tinker Road, which experiences high vehicle speeds. He added 
that the addition allows multi-generational living and matches 
the large residential structures in the neighborhood. 
MOTION by Mr. Nehiley to approve the variance application on 
behalf of the owners. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that granting the variance would not be 
contrary to the public interest because maintaining driveway 
access on Adella Drive rather than creating a new entrance on 
high-speed Tinker Road protects public safety. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that the spirit of the ordinance would be 
observed because large attached garages are customary in this R-
40 neighborhood, and the structure fits aesthetically with the 
home.
11 
 
Mr. Nehiley stated that granting the variance would do 
substantial justice because it allows the family to convert 
existing space for elderly parents to age in place while 
replacing required covered parking. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that surrounding property values would not be 
diminished by an architecturally matching garage addition on a 
large lot. 
Mr. Nehiley stated that owing to special conditions of the 
property, denial of the variance would result in unnecessary 
hardship because the home is situated on a corner lot with two 
required 40-foot front yard setbacks. The house sits far forward 
on the parcel, creating an artificial restriction along the 
secondary frontage of Tinker Road. There is no fair and 
substantial relationship between the 40-foot setback rule and 
its application to this secondary frontage, and the proposed 
residential garage is reasonable. 
SECONDED by Mr. Patry.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
7. Bissono 413 S Main St, LLC (Owner) 413 South Main Street 
(Sheet 110 Lot 28) requesting variance from Land Use Code 
Section 190-15, Table 15-1 (#102) to allow a personal service 
use. RA Zone, Ward 6. 
Voting on this case: Jay Minkarah Josh Nehiley JP Boucher Joseph 
Patry 
Attorney Brad Westgate, Welts, White & Fontaine, Nashua, NH, and 
owner Miguel Bissono presented the case. Attorney Westgate 
explained that the applicant seeks a use variance to permit a 
small 415-square-foot personal service use (specifically 
licensed aesthetician/skincare services) within three interior 
rooms of an existing 1,600-square-foot commercial office 
building. He noted that the Board granted a use variance in 2020 
to convert the former residential building into a commercial 
office, followed by Planning Board site plan approval. Due to 
shifts toward remote work in the insurance industry, the full 
office space is no longer needed. He emphasized that no exterior 
building or site changes are proposed, access remains via the 
approved lower driveway off the stub end of Eastman Street, and 
client appointments are scheduled one at a time.
12 
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR: Kayla Gutierrez, 73 Burke Street, Nashua, NH. 
Ms. Gutierrez, an employee, spoke in favor, noting Mr. Bissono’s 
commitment to maintaining a quiet, high-quality professional 
space. Mr. Minkarah read a letter of support from immediate 
abutter Hong Hai Gardiner, 411 South Main Street, Nashua, NH, 
stating that the property is meticulously maintained and the 
interior use change will have no negative impact. 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR WITH QUESTIONS OR CONCERNS: Cynthia 
Knowles, 15 Eastman Street, Nashua, NH. Mrs. Knowles expressed 
concern over traffic and pedestrian safety on Eastman Street, 
stating it is a narrow residential street with young children 
and frequent cut-through traffic. She argued that adding 
personal service clients will increase vehicle trips. 
Colleen Valente, 33 Eastman Street, Nashua, NH. Mrs. Valente 
cited ongoing traffic congestion, vehicles turning around in 
private driveways, and issues with snow plowing contractor 
vehicles blocking access along Eastman Street. 
Mr. Minkarah noted receipt of letters expressing concerns from 
Elise Lucas (4 Learned St), Isabel Bonenfant, and Colleen 
Valente. 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR – REBUTTAL: Attorney Westgate stated that the 
site plan approved by the Planning Board in 2020 authorized full 
commercial office use for the entire first floor. He emphasized 
that a 415-square-foot, single-practitioner aesthetician office 
operating by appointment generates equal or less traffic than 
permitted medical, legal, or accounting offices. He added that 
snow storage is designated on the approved site plan and the 
owner will ensure contractors comply. 
END OF PUBLIC HEARING, BEGINNING OF PUBLIC MEETING: Mr. Nehiley, 
Mr. Patry, Mr. Boucher, and Mr. Minkarah spoke in favor. Mr. 
Nehiley noted that the building exterior and parking layout 
remain unchanged, and appointment-based aesthetician services 
result in low vehicle turnover. He urged the owner to maintain 
good neighbor relations regarding snow storage along Eastman 
Street. Mr. Patry and Mr. Boucher agreed that a single 
aesthetician sees fewer clients per hour than traditional walk-
in office uses. Mr. Minkarah added that South Main Street is a 
heavily traveled commercial corridor with mixed non-residential 
uses, and converting interior office rooms to personal services 
creates no exterior impact.
13 
 
MOTION by Mr. Minkarah to approve the variance application on 
behalf of the owner as advertised. 
Mr. Minkarah stated that granting the variance would not be 
contrary to the public interest because the personal service use 
will be conducted entirely within an existing, approved 
commercial office building with no exterior or site 
modifications, preserving neighborhood character. 
Mr. Minkarah stated that the spirit of the ordinance would be 
observed because South Main Street contains a mix of commercial 
and office uses, and an appointment-only personal service use 
generates nominal traffic that will not injure public health, 
safety, or welfare. 
Mr. Minkarah stated that granting the variance would do 
substantial justice because the loss to the property owner of 
leaving approved commercial space vacant outweighs any minor, 
unproven concern to the public. 
Mr. Minkarah stated that there is no evidence that surrounding 
property values would be diminished, given that no physical site 
changes are occurring. 
Mr. Minkarah stated that owing to special conditions of the 
property, denial of the variance would result in unnecessary 
hardship because the property is an existing commercial office 
building situated on a heavily traveled mixed-use corridor with 
dual street access. Strictly prohibiting a minor personal 
service use within a pre-existing approved office layout is 
unreasonable, and there is no fair and substantial relationship 
between the general RA prohibition and its specific application 
to this commercial site. The proposed use is reasonable. 
SECONDED by Mr. Nehiley.  
MOTION TO APPROVE CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
 
OTHER BUSINESS: 
REGIONAL IMPACT: The Board reviewed the upcoming agenda and 
determined that none of the proposed cases present regional 
impact.
14 
 
MINUTES: The Board reviewed the draft minutes for the September 
9, 2026 public hearing and meeting. 
MOTION by Mr. Patry to approve the minutes of September 9, 2026 
as presented, waive the reading, and place the minutes in the 
file.  
SECONDED by Mr. Nehiley.  
MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY 4-0. 
ADJOURNMENT: MOTION by Mr. Patry to adjourn the meeting at 8:34 
PM.  
SECONDED by Mr. Nehiley.  
MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY. 
Submitted by: Sam Durfee, Planning Manager.
